app_documentation:
The Real-Time Inventory Management System is a comprehensive web and mobile application designed specifically for retail store environments to streamline inventory tracking, product management, and stock monitoring operations. The system enables store staff to efficiently manage their product catalog, track stock levels in real-time, and receive proactive alerts when inventory falls below predefined thresholds. Built with modern technologies including React for the frontend, Node.js/Express for the backend API, PostgreSQL for data persistence, and WebSocket for real-time updates, the application provides a responsive and intuitive user experience across both web and mobile platforms.

The application's core features include barcode scanning for rapid product identification and inventory updates, real-time inventory tracking with automatic stock level adjustments during sales and restocking operations, automated low stock alerts to prevent stockouts, comprehensive product management capabilities for adding and editing product information, and detailed sales reporting with data export functionality. The barcode scanning feature integrates with standard USB or Bluetooth scanner devices and mobile device cameras, allowing store clerks to quickly scan products and update inventory counts within seconds. The real-time tracking system uses WebSocket connections to ensure all users see immediate updates when inventory changes occur, maintaining data accuracy across the organization.

The system is designed to serve three distinct user roles with varying levels of access and permissions: Store Owners who have full system access including user management and business analytics, Store Managers who can manage inventory, configure alerts, and oversee daily operations, and Store Clerks who primarily handle product scanning and basic inventory updates. Each role is carefully designed with appropriate permissions to ensure data security while enabling efficient workflow execution. The application emphasizes speed and usability with features like quick scan buttons accessible from any screen, floating action buttons for common tasks, and a clean card-based interface that makes critical information immediately visible.

With its focus on real-time data visibility, proactive alert management, and streamlined workflows, the Real-Time Inventory Management System helps retail stores maintain optimal stock levels, reduce manual counting errors, improve reordering efficiency, and ultimately enhance customer satisfaction by ensuring products are always available when needed. The system's mobile-first design ensures that store staff can perform inventory operations anywhere in the store using handheld devices, while the web interface provides comprehensive reporting and management capabilities for office-based administrative tasks.

glossary.SKU: Stock Keeping Unit - A unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to each distinct product in the inventory system for tracking and management purposes. Each SKU must be unique across all products in the database.
glossary.Barcode Scanning: The process of using optical scanning technology (via USB/Bluetooth scanner devices or mobile device cameras) to read product barcodes and automatically retrieve product information and update inventory counts in the system within 2 seconds.
glossary.Low Stock Threshold: A configurable minimum quantity level set for each product that triggers automatic alert notifications when the current inventory falls below this value. Default threshold is 10 units but can be customized per product by managers or owners.
glossary.Real-Time Inventory Tracking: A system capability that uses WebSocket connections to immediately update and synchronize stock levels across all connected clients whenever inventory changes occur through sales, restocks, adjustments, or returns, ensuring all users see current data.
glossary.Transaction: A recorded event in the system representing any change to inventory levels, categorized by type (sale, restock, adjustment, return) and including details such as product, quantity changed, user who performed the action, timestamp, and optional notes.
glossary.Role-Based Access Control: A security mechanism that restricts system features and data access based on assigned user roles (Store Owner, Store Manager, Store Clerk), with each role having specific permissions for operations like product deletion, user management, and inventory adjustments.
